display.title: The Sound of the Shofar: An Alarm to Wake Us Up
display.summary_short: Why we blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah: the Rambam's 'alarm' that wakes us to crown Hashem as King and to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show in Elul. Uncle Yossi reminds children that the shofar is blown each weekday morning of Elul, and explains its message. The Torah commands us to sound the shofar on Rosh Hashanah without giving a reason, but the Rambam teaches that it hints to many lessons, above all that it is like an alarm that wakes a sleeper. On Rosh Hashanah we proclaim Hashem as our King and Father, pray to be written in the Book of Life, and resolve to do better in Torah and mitzvos. The shofar is an alarm for action: since all our deeds are weighed, we answer it with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah, and pray for a good, sweet year and for the great shofar that will announce Moshiach.
display.lesson: The shofar is a call to action: answer it with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
